parsed.reason: The reply does the job: it hands Sam the referral link (which is the appended runtime link, not an invented URL), explains in plain terms what to do with it (forward it), and gives a brief accurate description of what Hale is. The instruction that Hale never texts the friend is respected — the parent is told to forward it themselves. No greeting, no sign-off, no markdown, no questions, no app mention. The description "tracks your family's week - activities, schedules, deadlines" is accurate and useful context for a friend. The only small blemish is the opening "Here's your referral line to forward -" is a touch clunky/wordy when it could just lead with the purpose, but it is not wrong. A clean, correct reply that does exactly what was asked.
